scorecards.inningsCommentary: Sri Lanka commenced their first innings at SuperSport Park, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 85 from LD Chandimal, complemented by a commanding 131-run stand between Dhananjaya Silva and LD Chandimal that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 4.07 RPO. South Africa's bowling response was spearheaded by L Sipamla (5/73), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 396/10 (95.6 ov), Sri Lanka posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, Sri Lanka sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 64 from MDKJ Perera, complemented by a commanding 63-run stand between LD Chandimal and MDKJ Perera that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.84 RPO. L Sipamla (2/23) maintained tight lines for South Africa, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Sri Lanka's total of 180/9 (46.1 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at SuperSport Park commenced with high tactical intensity as Sri Lanka posted 396/10 (95.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, South Africa countered with 621/10 (142.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Francois Plessis 199 (278b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Francois Plessis delivered a masterclass for South Africa (199 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (South Africa 55%) and allowing South Africa to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. South Africa's bowling unit, bolstered by Pinnaduwage Silva (77 Runs & 4 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing South Africa won by innings & 45 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: South Africa's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, South Africa won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
